Prealgebra · Lesson 7.5

Converting Units

Solve this lesson →All lessons

When the top and bottom of a fraction are the same real amount in different units, that fraction equals 11. Such a fraction is a conversion factor. Multiplying by it swaps the unit label without changing the true quantity.

Problem
One hand equals 4 inches. A pony is 36 inches tall. Multiply by 1 hand4 in4in1hand​ so the inches cancel. How many hands tall is the pony?
Show a hint
  • A conversion factor is a fraction equal to 11 whose top and bottom are the same height in different units, so both 4 in1 hand1 hand4 in​ and 1 hand4 in4 in1 hand​ equal 11. You start with inches and want hands, so choose the one with inches on the bottom, 1 hand4 in4 in1 hand​. That way inches will cancel and hands will be the unit that survives.
  • Write the chain as 36 in×1 hand4 in36 in×4 in1 hand​. Cross out the inin on top against the inin on the bottom, then the unit left is hands. Now just do the number part, 36÷436÷4.
Show the full solution
Put inches on the bottom so they cancel and hands are left. 36 in×1 hand4 in=364 hands36 in×4 in1 hand​=436​ hands The pony is 99​ hands tall. Flip that factor the other way and the units come out as in2handhandin2​, which is how the units warn you the factor is upside down.
Problem
One fathom equals 6 feet. An anchor rope is 23 fathoms long. Using the factor 6 ft1 fathom1fathom6ft​, convert to feet. How many feet long is the rope?
Show a hint
  • Write the relationship as a fraction equal to 11. You want "fathom" to cancel, so the fathom unit needs to sit on the bottom of your conversion factor while feet sits on top, giving 6 ft1 fathom1 fathom6 ft​.
  • Multiply 23 fathom×6 ft1 fathom23 fathom×1 fathom6 ft​. The fathom labels cancel, then multiply 23×623×6. Whatever number you get carries the unit "ft".
Show the full solution
Put fathoms on the bottom so they cancel and feet are left. 23 fathom×6 ft1 fathom=23×6 ft=138 ft23 fathom×1 fathom6 ft​=23×6 ft=138 ft The rope is 138138​ feet long. That factor equals 11 because 6 feet and 1 fathom are the same distance, so it changes the label without changing the rope.
Problem
270 loose jars need to be packed into crates of 18. Use 1 crate18 jars18jars1crate​ so jars cancel and crates survive. How many full crates do 270 jars make?
Show a hint
  • You have two factors to pick from, 18 jars1 crate1 crate18 jars​ and 1 crate18 jars18 jars1 crate​, and both equal 11. The unit you are starting with is jars, and a unit cancels only when it shows up on the top of one fraction and the bottom of another. Since your 270270 jars is on top, the factor you choose must carry jars on the bottom so the two jars cancel and crates is left behind. Which of the two factors has jars underneath?
Show the full solution
Jars is the unit you want gone, so put it on the bottom. 270 jars×1 crate18 jars=27018 crates=15 crates270 jars×18 jars1 crate​=18270​ crates=15 crates So 270 jars fill 1515​ full crates. The other orientation would have left units of jars2cratecratejars2​, which is how the units catch a flipped factor.
Problem
One stone equals 14 pounds. Luggage weighs 91 pounds. Build a conversion factor so the pounds cancel and stone survives. What is the weight in stone? (The answer is not a whole number.)
Show a hint
  • You want pounds to cancel and stone to survive. Since 1 stone is 14 pounds, the factor 1 stone14 pounds14 pounds1 stone​ is just a ratio equal to 1. Multiplying by 1 never changes the true weight, it only changes the unit it is written in.
  • Write 91 pounds×1 stone14 pounds91 pounds×14 pounds1 stone​ and cross out the matching pound units. That leaves the number 91141491​ carrying the unit stone. Now reduce 91141491​ to lowest terms by dividing the top and bottom by their greatest common factor.
Show the full solution
Put pounds on the bottom so they cancel and stone is left. 91 pounds×1 stone14 pounds=9114 stone91 pounds×14 pounds1 stone​=1491​ stone Both numbers share a factor of 7, since 91=7×1391=7×13 and 14=7×214=7×2, so the luggage weighs 13/213/2​ stone, the same as 6.5 stone. Conversion factors work just as well when the answer lands between two whole numbers.
Key idea
A conversion factor equals 1. It is a fraction whose top and bottom are the exact same real amount in two different units, like 12 in1 ft1ft12in​. That is one amount divided by itself, so it equals 11, and multiplying by it changes the unit label and not the quantity. Every fact gives two factors, the fraction and its reciprocal, and both equal 11. Put the unit you want removed on the bottom so it cancels and the unit you want is left. The leftover unit confirms you wrote the factor correctly.
Problem
A racecourse is 4 furlongs. Use 1 furlong=220 yd1furlong=220yd and 1 yd=3 ft1yd=3ft. Chain two factors through yards. How many feet is 4 furlongs?
Show a hint
  • You cannot jump straight from furlongs to feet, so hop through yards in the middle. Build the first conversion factor from 1 furlong=220 yards1 furlong=220 yards, and orient it so the unit you want to get rid of, furlongs, sits on the bottom. That makes it 220 yd1 furlong1 furlong220 yd​, and since top and bottom are the same length, this fraction equals 11, so multiplying by it changes the unit without changing the actual distance.
  • Now line up the whole chain so each factor cancels the unit the one before it produced. Write 4 furlong×220 yd1 furlong×3 ft1 yd4 furlong×1 furlong220 yd​×1 yd3 ft​. The furlongs cancel against the first bottom and the yards cancel against the second bottom, leaving feet. Then just multiply the numbers across, 4×220×34×220×3.
Show the full solution
No single furlong-to-feet factor exists, so chain two through yards, each turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 4 furlong×220 yd1 furlong×3 ft1 yd=4×220×3 ft4 furlong×1 furlong220 yd​×1 yd3 ft​=4×220×3 ft Furlong cancels against the first denominator and yard against the second, leaving feet, and 4×220×3=2,6404×220×3=2,640. So 4 furlongs is 26402640​ feet.
Problem
A bolt of cloth is 6 yards long. Using 1 yd=3 ft1yd=3ft and 1 ft=12 in1ft=12in, chain two factors. How many inches long is the cloth?
Show a hint
  • You have no single yard-to-inch factor, so build a bridge through feet. Start with the factor that kills yards. Since 11 yard =3=3 feet, write it as 3 ft1 yd1 yd3 ft​ so that the "yd" on top of 6 yd6 yd cancels the "yd" on the bottom of the factor, leaving feet.
  • Now stack a second factor that kills feet. Use 12 in1 ft1 ft12 in​ so "ft" cancels and only "in" survives. The whole chain is 6 yd×3 ft1 yd×12 in1 ft6 yd×1 yd3 ft​×1 ft12 in​. Multiply the numbers across, 6×3×126×3×12.
Show the full solution
There is no yard-to-inch fact, so chain two factors through feet. 6 yd×3 ft1 yd×12 in1 ft=6×3×12 in6 yd×1 yd3 ft​×1 ft12 in​=6×3×12 in The yd cancels, then the ft cancels, and only in survives. The cloth is 216216​ inches long.
Problem
A lantern festival lasts 1 fortnight (14 days). Using 1 day=24 hr1day=24hr and 1 hr=60 min1hr=60min, convert through three factors. How many minutes long is 1 fortnight?
Show a hint
  • Start with 1 fortnight1 fortnight and multiply by a conversion factor that puts fortnightfortnight on the bottom so it cancels. Since 1 fortnight=14 days1 fortnight=14 days, that first factor is 14 days1 fortnight1 fortnight14 days​, which is just a ratio equal to 1. Now you are holding days, and you need to keep relaying down to minutes.
  • Chain all three factors in a row, each one cancelling the unit before it. Write 1 fortnight×14 days1 fortnight×24 hr1 day×60 min1 hr1 fortnight×1 fortnight14 days​×1 day24 hr​×1 hr60 min​ and multiply the top numbers, 14×24×6014×24×60. Notice 14×24=33614×24=336, then 336×60336×60.
Show the full solution
Chain three factors, each turned so the unwanted unit sits on the bottom. 1 fortnight×14 days1 fortnight×24 hr1 day×60 min1 hr1 fortnight×1 fortnight14 days​×1 day24 hr​×1 hr60 min​ Fortnight, day, and hr each cancel in turn, leaving minutes. Then 14×24=33614×24=336 and 336×60=20,160336×60=20,160, so 1 fortnight is 2016020160​ minutes.
Problem
An arcade: 1 dollar buys 4 tokens, and 1 token buys 3 prize tickets. No direct dollar-to-ticket rate is posted. Chain two factors through tokens. How many prize tickets are 9 dollars worth?
Show a hint
  • You want to start with 9 dollars9 dollars and end with tickets, so build conversion factors that cancel what you do not want. Each given exchange is a ratio equal to 11, and you can flip it either way. Pick the orientation with "dollars" on the bottom for the first factor, 4 tokens1 dollar1 dollar4 tokens​, so the dollars divide out.
  • Dollars alone cannot reach tickets, so chain a second factor that has tokens on the bottom, 3 tickets1 token1 token3 tickets​. Now write the whole product, 9 dollars×4 tokens1 dollar×3 tickets1 token9 dollars×1 dollar4 tokens​×1 token3 tickets​, cross out dollars then tokens, and multiply the numbers 9×4×39×4×3.
Show the full solution
Chain the two exchanges through tokens, each factor turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 9 dollars×4 tokens1 dollar×3 tickets1 token=9×4×3 tickets9 dollars×1 dollar4 tokens​×1 token3 tickets​=9×4×3 tickets Dollars cancel, then tokens cancel, and only tickets survive, so 9 dollars is worth 108108​ prize tickets. A posted exchange rate is a conversion factor like any other.
Fun fact
In 1999 NASA lost the $300$300-million Mars Climate Orbiter because one team sent pound-force seconds while the software expected newton seconds, off by 4.45. A conversion error destroyed a spacecraft.
Key idea
Chaining conversion factors. When no single factor connects your starting unit to the one you want, go through a middle unit and multiply by several factors in a row. Every factor equals 11, so the whole chain still multiplies by 11, and the real amount does not change. Write each factor so the unit you just produced is on the bottom and cancels, until only the target unit is left. Exchange rates and prices work the same way. A rate like ‘17 pesos per dollar’ is a ratio you can flip, so it is another conversion factor.
Problem
A cyclist rides at 45 miles per hour. Use 1 mi=5,280 ft1mi=5,280ft and 1 hr=3,600 s1hr=3,600s to convert. What is the speed in feet per second?
Show a hint
  • A conversion factor is a ratio equal to 11, so multiplying by it never changes the speed, only its dress. You have miles on top and you want feet on top, so use 5,280 ft1 mi1 mi5,280 ft​ with the mile on the bottom, ready to cancel the mile in 45 mi1 hr1 hr45 mi​. Separately, you have hours on the bottom and you want seconds on the bottom, so you will need a factor that puts hours on top to cancel them.
  • Chain all three pieces together, 45 mi1 hr×5,280 ft1 mi×1 hr3,600 s1 hr45 mi​×1 mi5,280 ft​×3,600 s1 hr​. The miles cancel and the hours cancel, leaving feet over seconds. Now just the numbers remain, 45×5,2803,6003,60045×5,280​, which is 237,6003,6003,600237,600​.
Show the full solution
Write the speed as a fraction and attach two factors, one for the top unit and one for the bottom. 45 mi1 hr×5,280 ft1 mi×1 hr3,600 s=45×5,2803,600 ft/s1 hr45 mi​×1 mi5,280 ft​×3,600 s1 hr​=3,60045×5,280​ ft/s The mi cancels and the hr cancels, leaving feet over seconds, and 237,6003,600=663,600237,600​=66. The speed is 6666​ ft/s.
Problem
A syrup has density 1.5 g/mL1.5g/mL. A tank holds 4 liters. Convert liters to mL, then apply the density. How many grams of syrup does the tank hold?
Show a hint
  • The density 1.5 g1 mL1 mL1.5 g​ is built for milliliters, but your volume is in liters. Before you can use it, turn 44 liters into milliliters with a conversion factor that cancels liters, oriented as 1000 mL1 liter1 liter1000 mL​ so "liter" is on the bottom.
  • Build the full chain 4 liters×1000 mL1 liter×1.5 g1 mL4 liters×1 liter1000 mL​×1 mL1.5 g​. The first factor cancels liters and the second cancels milliliters, leaving grams. Now just multiply the numbers, 4×1000×1.54×1000×1.5.
Show the full solution
Send liters to milliliters first, then let the density turn milliliters into grams, each factor turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 4 liters×1000 mL1 liter×1.5 g1 mL4 liters×1 liter1000 mL​×1 mL1.5 g​ Liter cancels, then mL cancels, leaving grams. Since 4×1000=40004×1000=4000 and 4000×1.5=60004000×1.5=6000, the tank holds 60006000​ grams. A density is a conversion factor too, one that trades volume for mass.
Key idea
Converting a rate needs two factors. A rate has one unit on top and a different unit underneath, so a single factor only changes one of them. Multiply by two factors, one for the top unit and one for the bottom unit. Write each factor so its unwanted unit cancels with the matching unit in the rate. The units left on top and on the bottom are the converted rate.
Problem
A sticker covers 12 square inches. Use 1 in=2.5 cm1in=2.5cm. The factor must be applied twice since area is length ×× length. How many square centimeters is the sticker?
Show a hint
  • A conversion factor is a ratio equal to 11. Here the relationship 1 in=2.5 cm1 in=2.5 cm gives the factor 2.5 cm1 in1 in2.5 cm​. But the unit you are converting is square inches, which is in×inin×in, so a single cminincm​ only cancels one of the two inches. What happens to the leftover inch?
  • Multiply by the factor 2.5 cm1 in1 in2.5 cm​ twice, once for each side of the little square. Watch both inch units cancel and two centimeter units appear. Then the number part is 12×2.5×2.512×2.5×2.5, so the linear factor 2.52.5 is squared.
Show the full solution
A square inch is 1 in×1 in1 in×1 in, so the factor 2.5 cm1 in1 in2.5 cm​ gets used twice, once for each side. 12 in2×2.5 cm1 in×2.5 cm1 in12 in2×1 in2.5 cm​×1 in2.5 cm​ Both inch units cancel and two centimeter units are left, which make cm2cm2. Then 2.5×2.5=6.252.5×2.5=6.25 and 12×6.25=7512×6.25=75, so the sticker is 7575​ square centimeters. Using the linear factor twice is the same as squaring it.
Problem
On a game island: 1 brindle=5 floons1brindle=5floons, 1 floon=4 ticks1floon=4ticks, 1 tick=6 motes1tick=6motes. A path is 3 brindles long. How many motes?
Show a hint
  • You have no idea how big a brindle or a mote really is, and that is fine. The method runs on the relationships alone. Start with 3 brindle3 brindle and pick the first conversion factor so that brindle cancels, which means brindle goes on the bottom, 5 floons1 brindle1 brindle5 floons​.
  • Keep going one unit at a time, floon to tick to mote, each new factor oriented so the unit you just made lands on the bottom and cancels. After every cancellation only motes survive, so multiply the top numbers, 3×5×4×63×5×4×6.
Show the full solution
Lay the three facts down as factors, each turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom, and walk brindle to floon to tick to mote. 3 brindle×5 floons1 brindle×4 ticks1 floon×6 motes1 tick3 brindle×1 brindle5 floons​×1 floon4 ticks​×1 tick6 motes​ Brindle, floon, and tick each cancel, leaving motes, and 3×5×4×6=3603×5×4×6=360. The path is 360360​ motes long. You never had to picture any of these units, only the relationships between them.
Key idea
Area uses the conversion factor twice. An area is a length times a length, so each length needs its own conversion factor, and using it twice is the same as squaring it. If 1 unit=k1unit=k of another, then 11 square unit =k2=k2 square units, not just kk. Every conversion works the same way. Single steps, long chains, money, speeds, densities, areas, and invented units are all multiplication by a fraction that equals 11, written so the unwanted unit cancels.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In the highlands, 1 league equals 3 miles. The Ridgeback Trail is 8 leagues long. How many miles long is the trail?
Show the solution
Put leagues on the bottom so they cancel and miles are left. 8 leagues×3 miles1 league=8×3 miles=24 miles8 leagues×1 league3 miles​=8×3 miles=24 miles The trail is 2424​ miles long.
Practice
One gross equals 144 pencils. A warehouse has 360 loose pencils. How many gross is that?
Show the solution
Put pencils on the bottom so they cancel and gross is left. 360 pencils×1 gross144 pencils=360144 gross360 pencils×144 pencils1 gross​=144360​ gross Both numbers share the factor 7272, and 360÷72=5360÷72=5 while 144÷72=2144÷72=2, so the warehouse has 5/25/2​ gross, which is two and a half gross.
Practice
One ream equals 500 sheets. A dock has 3,500 sheets. Using the factor 1 ream500 sheets500sheets1ream​, how many reams is that?
Show the solution
Start with the amount you have and multiply by the conversion factor oriented so sheets cancels. 3,500 sheets×1 ream500 sheets=3,500500 reams3,500 sheets×500 sheets1 ream​=5003,500​ reams The unit sheets appears on top and bottom, so it cancels and reams remains. Now divide. 3,500500=75003,500​=7 So 3,5003,500 sheets is 77​ reams.
Practice
Each brick is 9 inches long. A wall is 162 inches long. Using the factor 1 brick9 in9in1brick​ so the inches cancel, how many bricks long is the wall?
Show the solution
Start with the wall length and attach the conversion factor with inches on the bottom, so the inches cancel and bricks are left. 162 in×1 brick9 in162 in×9 in1 brick​ The inch units cancel, top and bottom. 162 in×1 brick9 in=1629 bricks162 in×9 in1 brick​=9162​ bricks Now divide. 1629=18 bricks9162​=18 bricks So the wall is 1818​ bricks long.
Practice
A surveyor has 1 mile=8 furlongs1mile=8furlongs and 1 furlong=40 rods1furlong=40rods. A boundary is 2 miles. Chain two factors and convert to rods. How many rods long is the boundary?
Show the solution
Chain two factors through furlongs, each turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 2 mile×8 furlong1 mile×40 rod1 furlong=2×8×40 rod2 mile×1 mile8 furlong​×1 furlong40 rod​=2×8×40 rod Mile cancels, then furlong cancels, leaving rods. The boundary is 640640​ rods long.
Practice
A recipe needs 5 gallons of water, measured in pints. Given 1 gal=4 qt1gal=4qt and 1 qt=2 pt1qt=2pt, chain two factors. How many pints are in 5 gallons?
Show the solution
Start with 55 gallons and chain two conversion factors so the unwanted units cancel. Orient each factor with the unit you want to remove on the bottom. 5 gallon×4 quart1 gallon×2 pint1 quart5 gallon×1 gallon4 quart​×1 quart2 pint​ The gallons cancel against the gallon on the bottom of the first factor, and the quarts cancel against the quart on the bottom of the second factor, leaving only pints. 5×4×2=40 pint5×4×2=40 pint So 55 gallons is 4040​ pints.
Practice
How many seconds are in 1 full day? Chain three factors using 1 day=24 hr1day=24hr, 1 hr=60 min1hr=60min, 1 min=60 s1min=60s.
Show the solution
Chain three factors, each turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 1 day×24 hours1 day×60 minutes1 hour×60 seconds1 minute=24×60×60 seconds1 day×1 day24 hours​×1 hour60 minutes​×1 minute60 seconds​=24×60×60 seconds Day, hour, and minute each cancel, leaving seconds. One full day holds 8640086400​ seconds.
Practice
A collection is 3 stacks. Each stack holds 5 bundles, each bundle holds 4 packs, each pack holds 12 cards. Chain three factors and convert stacks to cards. How many cards is that?
Show the solution
Chain one factor per step, each turned so the old unit cancels. 3 stacks×5 bundles1 stack×4 packs1 bundle×12 cards1 pack3 stacks×1 stack5 bundles​×1 bundle4 packs​×1 pack12 cards​ Stacks, bundles, and packs all cancel, leaving cards, and 3×5×4×12=7203×5×4×12=720. The collection holds 720720​ cards.
Practice
A festival booth exchanges 1 euro for 12 ride tokens. A visitor exchanges 15 euros. Using the factor 12 tokens1 euro1euro12tokens​, how many tokens does the visitor get?
Show the solution
Put euros on the bottom of the factor so they cancel and tokens are left. 15 euros×12 tokens1 euro=15×12 tokens=180 tokens15 euros×1 euro12 tokens​=15×12 tokens=180 tokens The visitor gets 180180​ ride tokens.
Practice
A summer fair: 1 dollar buys 20 game chips, and 1 chip earns 3 prize points. A guest exchanges 7 dollars. Chain two factors through chips. How many prize points is that worth?
Show the solution
Chain the two exchanges through chips, each factor turned so the unwanted unit is on the bottom. 7 dollars×20 chips1 dollar×3 points1 chip=7×20×3 points7 dollars×1 dollar20 chips​×1 chip3 points​=7×20×3 points Dollars cancel, then chips cancel, leaving points. So 7 dollars is worth 420420​ prize points.
Practice
A maglev train travels at 72 km/hr. Convert to m/s using 1 km=1,000 m1km=1,000m and 1 hr=3,600 s1hr=3,600s. What is the speed in meters per second?
Show the solution
Attach one factor for the top unit and one for the bottom, each turned so the unwanted unit cancels. 72 km1 hr×1,000 m1 km×1 hr3,600 s=72×1,0003,600 m/s1 hr72 km​×1 km1,000 m​×3,600 s1 hr​=3,60072×1,000​ m/s The km cancels and the hr cancels, leaving meters over seconds, and 72,0003,600=203,60072,000​=20. The train moves at 2020​ meters per second.
Practice
A runner's pace is 15 mph. Convert to feet per minute using 1 mi=5,280 ft1mi=5,280ft and 1 hr=60 min1hr=60min. What is the speed in feet per minute?
Show the solution
Use 5,280 ft1 mi1 mi5,280 ft​ to clear the miles on top and 1 hr60 min60 min1 hr​ to clear the hours on the bottom. 15 mi1 hr×5,280 ft1 mi×1 hr60 min=15×5,28060 ft/min1 hr15 mi​×1 mi5,280 ft​×60 min1 hr​=6015×5,280​ ft/min Feet over minutes is what survives, and 79,20060=1,3206079,200​=1,320. The runner is moving at 13201320​ feet per minute.
Practice
A jar holds 8 tablespoons of maple syrup. The density is 21 g1 tablespoon1tablespoon21g​. How many grams of syrup does the jar hold?
Show the solution
Start with the amount you know and attach the density as a conversion factor, oriented so tablespoons cancels and grams stays. 8 tablespoons×21 g1 tablespoon8 tablespoons×1 tablespoon21 g​ The tablespoontablespoon on top cancels with the tablespoontablespoon on the bottom. 8 tablespoons×21 g1 tablespoon=(8×21) g8tablespoons​×1tablespoon​21 g​=(8×21) g Now finish the multiplication, 8×21=1688×21=168, and the only surviving unit is grams. So the jar holds 168168​ grams of syrup.
Practice
A workshop floor covers 6 square feet. Convert to square inches using 1 ft=12 in1ft=12in. Remember the linear factor gets applied twice for area. What is the area in square inches?
Show the solution
Use the factor 12 in1 ft1 ft12 in​ twice, since an area carries two lengths. 6 ft2×12 in1 ft×12 in1 ft=6×12×12 in26 ft2×1 ft12 in​×1 ft12 in​=6×12×12 in2 The ft2ft2 cancels against the two ftft on the bottom, leaving in2in2, and 6×144=8646×144=864. The floor is 864864​ square inches.
